I'm a NEET and college dropout with $50k in the bank.

Open thread • Replies: 36 • Updated: 2026-07-30 21:18 UTC

OP

I've given up and I do not care. My mom wants me to get it together so I can get us a house. I just don't care bros. When single wide homes are going for $300k what's the point of doing anything? Literally, I'm looking at a local single wide that goes for $375k and it's on a 1.09 acre lot. It's all a bubble in the end. "It's not a bubble because people need a home." I have a home. It may be a 41 year old trailer but it's a home. My mom doesn't seem to get that. "Why did you drop out?" Because college is meaningless and soul crushing. I can't do it and I won't do it. The last job I worked was Lowe's home improvement in 2020. I couldn't do it either being a wagie is so soulless. Because for me if the job has no meaning, and most jobs don't, what's the point of working? For money? Why trade your soul for money? Hell, even if the job had meaning it would be meaningless. Trading your time for money is inherently soulless.

"H-How did you get 50k anon?!" I got lucky on shitcoins. I did small trades of a thousand here and there and the meme coins went up. But look, I just don't care. I could have a million bucks and I'd realize something profound. It's just a carrot on a stick. And it never ends. You always want more. But I think, in a world filled with material desire and the fleeting chase of wealth, the only true wealth is wanting less. Having less. Not everyone can reconcile the meaningless nature of everything a human being "has" to do in this life. I am one of them. Because if you really believe nothing has any meaning like I do you're just stunlocked. You can't do anything, you won't do anything. However, in a weird way meaning may still be forged.

A note from Gavin Wood

"A short note on where I am spending my time.

It has been a long road, but the recent chapters tell a simple story. In 2022 I stepped back from running Parity to bury myself in the deep protocol and architecture work, the designing and thinking I have always been happiest doing. Last year I picked up the reins as CEO because that groundwork was laid and the world was finally ready for it. The architecture is defined and the bar is set. Now the job is to deliver, and that is where I intend to put my attention.

In practice that means leading the technical side of delivery directly, taking the proofs of concept we have laboured over and hardening them into robust, open-source software that people can actually use. It is the part of the work I know best and care about most, and it is also precisely what this next phase calls for.

This comes as Pierre Aubert moves on after almost three years as VP of Engineering. In that time Pierre steered the engineering team through one of the most consequential periods of change in Parity's history, and kept us focused throughout on delivering the technologies that underpin Polkadot's future. He leaves the team in good shape, and with our genuine thanks I wish him every success in whatever he turns to next.

For everyone building with us, nothing about our direction changes and your day to day carries on as before. With an able team around me running the business, I can put my time where it counts most, and you will simply see me closer to the work as we ship.

This is the most interesting stretch of the journey so far. We've spent years laying the foundations; now comes the far better part, proving what they make possible and building the technology that leaves the internet more open, more resilient, and rather more human than we found it."
